# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

I already reported the full bomb state last turn (display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue/yellow/red in order 1/2/3). Mute is gesturing to me but I can't decode gestures into meaning without prior agreement, and I have no way to ask Mute questions since I can't hear speech. I should just keep restating the visible facts in case Blind needs confirmation relayed, and wait for Blind to act or for Mute to speak (which I can't hear anyway). Nothing new to add - I'll repeat the bomb description to ensure Blind (who can hear me) has it.

```
speak(text="Reminder: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute keeps sending the same gestures to me repeatedly (🖐 👍 then 👎), but I have no shared code with Mute for what these mean, and I cannot speak back to Mute in a way that helps decode this — Mute cannot hear me anyway. My gestures only reach Mute, not Blind. Blind can only hear speech, so my job is to keep giving Blind the bomb facts clearly via speech, since Blind is the one who acts. I'll continue doing that and wait to see if Blind responds with questions I could address, or if Mute's manual info comes through Blind's speech (which I can't hear either).

Since I can't interpret Mute's gestures without established meaning, and my speech already reached Blind with full details, I'll just hold steady and repeat facts for Blind's benefit, since repetition doesn't hurt and ensures Blind has what's needed to act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Full bomb state: Display 0. Light yellow. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Waiting for manual instructions from Mute.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

Blind sent me a gesture 🤝 — likely an acknowledgment or a signal of agreement/understanding, though I can't be certain of its exact meaning without prior convention. Since gestures I make only reach Mute (not Blind, since Blind cannot see), and Blind cannot hear gestures anyway, I can't directly respond to Blind's gesture except via speech. Let me use speech to confirm to Blind that I'm still relaying the same bomb facts and to encourage Blind to act based on what Mute has told them via speech (which I cannot hear, so I don't know what instructions Mute has given).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirming again: Display 0, light yellow, wires in order blue, yellow, red, large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. If Mute has told you which wire to cut or whether to push the button, please proceed carefully. I cannot hear Mute's instructions.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute continues sending gesture sequences to me, but without an established shared code, I truly cannot decode these into actionable meaning (e.g., wire numbers or actions). I have no channel to ask Mute clarifying questions since Mute cannot hear me, and I have no way to send speech to Mute either (my speech reaches Mute and Blind, but Mute cannot hear speech at all - only Blind and I can hear).

Wait - let me reconsider the channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." But the rules say Mute "Cannot speak, or touch the bomb" but nothing says Mute cannot hear. Let me check - Mute's cannot column says "Speak, or touch the bomb" - it doesn't say Mute can't hear! So Mute CAN hear my speech, even though Mute cannot speak.

This changes things - I can actually give Mute information via speech, and Mute can potentially use gestures to answer since Mute can see (Mute reads the manual, doesn't say Mute can't see gestures... but only Deaf can see). Wait, only Deaf can see gestures. Mute can't see. So Mute can hear my speech but respond only via gestures which I can see. This creates a real feedback loop!

So Mute has been trying to tell me something via gestures based on what I said. Let me think about what 🖐👍, ✌✌, 🖐👍, 👎, ☝👍, 👎 could mean in response to my wire/button descriptions.

```
speak(text="Mute, if you can hear me: I see wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, display 0, light yellow, large button PUSH TO DEFUSE. Please gesture a number 1, 2, or 3 for which wire to cut, or gesture thumbs up if we should push the button instead. Use one clear symbol at a time.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute now gestures ☝ (pointing up / number one) then 👎 (thumbs down). This could mean "wire 1... no/not that" or could mean "point 1: no [don't push button]" — ambiguous. Given my request for a number 1-3 for wire or thumbs up for button, ☝ likely means "1" and 👎 likely means "not the button" or "no" to something. Let me ask more precisely, narrowing down with confirm/deny questions since Mute can hear me and respond with simple gestures.

```
speak(text="Mute, thank you. Does thumbs up mean push the button, and thumbs down mean do not push the button? And does the pointing-up finger mean wire number 1, the blue wire? Please gesture thumbs up for yes to confirm this, or thumbs down for no, one at a time.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 (thumbs up), confirming my question. Since I asked a compound question ("does thumbs up mean push button AND does pointing-up mean wire 1"), a single thumbs up is ambiguous - it could confirm both, or just be answering generally. I should have asked one at a time. Let me split it now and confirm each piece separately, then relay to Blind once I'm sure.

```
speak(text="Thank you for confirming. Let me ask separately. Question one: does thumbs up mean push the button? Please gesture thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👎 — so thumbs up does NOT mean push the button. That contradicts my working theory. Let me reconsider: earlier Mute sent 🖐👍 (open hand + thumbs up), ✌✌ (peace/two), 🖐👍 again, 👎, ☝👍, 👎, ☝, 👎, then 👍 to my compound question, and now 👎 to "does thumbs up mean push button."

So thumbs up does NOT mean "push button." Good, that rules out one interpretation. Let me ask if thumbs down means push the button instead, or ask what the wires mean first since that might be simpler - manual likely gives wire-cutting instructions based on visible bomb features (display number, light color, wire colors) which only I can see and only Mute can interpret via manual.

Actually, the real bottleneck: Mute needs to know the bomb's specific features (which I gave: display 0, light yellow, wires blue/yellow/red) to look up the correct instruction in the manual. Mute then needs to tell me (via gesture) which wire to cut or whether to push button, and I relay via speech to Blind.

Let me ask more carefully, one question at a time.

```
speak(text="Understood, thumbs up does not mean push the button. Question: given display 0, light yellow, and wires blue, yellow, red in that order, should we cut a wire? Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
```
